d3_intro_1.speaker: Narration
d3_intro_1.text: A voicemail, left sometime in the night. A name they haven't said aloud in years. "It's been too long. Call me back?"

d3_intro_2.speaker: Narration
d3_intro_2.text: The old pull is there — to smooth it over, to make everyone comfortable. But comfort was never quite the same as safe.

d3_prep.speaker: Narration
d3_prep.text: There's a moment, finger over the call button. How to walk into this?

choices.text: Decide the limits now, while it's still quiet.
Rehearse every reply, brace for every angle.

d3_intro_3.speaker: Narration
d3_intro_3.text: If they call back, someone will have to hold the line — kindly, but firmly. Who can do that?

d3_out_iris.speaker: Iris
d3_out_iris.text: "It's good to hear from you. And — I need us to talk differently than we used to." Calm, unhurried. A boundary set without a single raised voice.

d3_out_rowan.speaker: Rowan
d3_out_rowan.text: He has the lines ready and delivers them cleanly — maybe a little clipped. The boundary holds, even if it lands more like a wall than a door.

d3_out_june.speaker: June
d3_out_june.text: She wants so badly to keep the peace that the line blurs, and the old patterns ease back in. Afterward, she is quiet for a long while.

d3_done.speaker: Narration
d3_done.text: The call ends. Whatever was said, the line stayed where they put it. That's new. That's theirs.
